explanation: King Ezana of Aksum, in modern Ethiopia and Eritrea, adopted Christianity in the 4th century, more than two centuries before Pope Gregory sent Augustine to Kent in 597.

claims.text: King Ezana of Aksum adopted Christianity in the 4th century, around the 330s or 340s.
Augustine's mission, sent by Pope Gregory I, reached Kent, in England, in 597.
The kingdom of Aksum lay in modern Ethiopia and Eritrea.
Ezana's conversion came more than two centuries before Augustine reached Kent, by calculation from c1 and c2.
